body:
The wiki describing itself rather than Dan. Three kinds of page live here: the
on-site mirrors of the root reading aids, the cross-model skills database, and
curated cross-domain journeys.

## Reading aids

Generated by `bin/wiki-digest` from the rest of the corpus — mirrors of
`DIGEST.md`, `RECENT.md`, `OPEN.md` at the repo root, given a `wiki/` address
so the portal actually serves them (its sync only reads `wiki/**` and
`sage/questions/**`).

- [[wiki/meta/digest]] — the front door: counts, altitude, the top of both lists below
- [[wiki/meta/recent-activity]] — what changed lately, and why
- [[wiki/meta/open-questions]] — every unresolved contradiction, gap and prediction

## The skills database

Not about Dan at all — about the machines that write these pages. Several
models work on this repository and none can see what the others have; this is
the shared record they push their skills, MCP servers, plugin tools and
subagents into. Generated by `bin/wiki-skills page` from an append-only log
under `skills/registry/`.

- [[wiki/meta/skills]] — every capability on the record, and how a model adds to it

## The plain-language edition

Every entry here is written for a reader who already knows the corpus. The
Reader's Digest is the same finding told to somebody who has never read
anything else, and the EDITION switch in the header is where you read it. This
tracks how much of the wiki has one. Generated by `bin/wiki-plain report` from
the tree and the git log.

- [[wiki/meta/readers-digest]] — coverage, the two writing lanes, and who wrote what

## Instruments — the measurement layer

Every other page here argues; these measure. Tools built to read something
about Dan out of first-party dated data, publishing **evidence and no finding**,
generated so a hand-edit fails the gate, and each stating what it structurally
cannot see. The section is the catalogue over them — the pages themselves live
in the domains they belong to, an intake ledger in `health` and a testimony
ledger in `meta`.

- [[wiki/meta/instruments/index]] — the ledgers, the measures, what the layer as a whole is blind to, and how to add one

## The veracity ledger

The wiki reasons from what a person said about himself. This is the record of
how often that has turned out to be so — every first-person assertion the
corpus has checked, what settled it, and the arithmetic over the settled ones.
Evidence, not a claim: it states no finding, and is regenerated by
`bin/wiki-testimony page` from an append-only log under `testimony/`.

- [[wiki/meta/testimony-veracity]] — the trust score, what his confidence is worth, and how the errors run

## Journeys

- [[wiki/meta/journeys/index]] — curated reading paths through several pages at once
